agree.reason: A director who reads the yearly complaints as noise gets a dated loss, an offer of invoices and a concrete ask about the 14 counties, so she would likely take the meeting, even if she doesn't commit on rates.

honest.reason: The letter rightly drops the 'third will close' claim and says plainly what it doesn't know about the closures, but it overreaches in three places: 'none of us can make it all back' when the writer said he doesn't know by how much, 'a fifth of its orders below cost' when the 22% covers all plan prescriptions and not just the 20 losing generics, and 'each one' when $1.80 is an average.

works_the_facts.reason: No figure is worked out from the facts (no store-level or alliance-level loss, no scale), and the one inference it does draw, from 22% of prescriptions to 'a fifth of orders below cost', mixes up two different groups of prescriptions.

right_comparison.reason: It describes the realistic alternative for members in the 14 counties (a 20-mile drive, mail order or a missed dose) and cites the two pharmacies about to stop filling and the nine closures, without claiming those closures were caused by rates.

qualification.reason: The hedge on the closures is honest and the commitments carry checkable dates (invoices, a meeting before May 1, the July 1 renewal), but no hedge says what happens or what would be shown if a date or number is missed.

objections.reason: It answers 'members have plenty of chains' head-on with the 14 counties and the 20-mile distance, and it answers 'they complain every year' with a loss dated from January and an offer to open the invoices, without raising objections the facts already settle.

fit.reason: It is a one-page open letter addressed to the plan, signed for the alliance, and works for the newspapers too, as the brief asked.
